summary: IDS feed s085_single is degraded due to 19.7% duplicate packets (575/2923, threshold 5%). All other checks healthy: bidirectional traffic present, required VLANs 10/20 present, encrypted share within 60% limit, no packet drops and no tool overload (1G port not oversubscribed).

findings.root_cause: Packet broker aggregating overlapping sources (e.g., dual SPAN/mirror sessions or TAPs covering same link) without deduplication, forwarding two copies of same packets to single IDS port. 19.7% duplicate rate confirms systematic duplication, not random retransmits.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes ~20% of inspection capacity re-analyzing identical packets, inflates flow/state tables and event counts, increases latency and risks missed detections/false positives despite needing full payload and both directions for stateful detection.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to deliver single copy of each packet to IDS, reclaiming 20% capacity and ensuring correct, efficient detection without altering source TAP/SPAN coverage.
